blocks.text: `consume` hands **ownership** of the data to the function. After the call that variable is **invalid**; it cannot be read. This way the same memory cannot be freed from two places and no "dangling" reference remains. You do not write `consume` at the call, only on the parameter.
Above, `hero` was invalid after `archive(hero)`; the new assignment brought it back to life. If you had written `print(hero.health)` right after `archive`, you would have got a compile error.

blocks.prompt: For `Task` (`title: str`) write `finish(t: consume Task)`: it prints `done: ` followed by the title. Call it in `main`.
blocks.hint: Add `finish` that does `print("done:", t.title)` and call `finish(t)` in `main`.

blocks.q: What happens to a variable that was `consume`d, after the call?
options: It can be used as before
It becomes invalid; it cannot be read until assigned again
blocks.why: Ownership passed to the function; the old variable no longer has the data.
